claim: Global/sequence-level Platt-scaling calibration, though effective for many generative software-engineering tasks, is unreliable or unexplored for automated code revision (ACR) tasks such as program repair, vulnerability repair, and code refinement.
stance_target: coarse-grained calibration is insufficient for code-revision tasks where correctness is locally determined
scope_conditions: automated code revision tasks: program repair, vulnerability repair, code refinement
quoted_support: global Platt-scaling of sequence-level confidence scores proving effective in many generative software engineering tasks but remaining unreliable or unexplored for automated code revision (ACR) tasks

claim: Fine-grained confidence scores calibrated with local Platt-scaling consistently achieve lower calibration error across a broader range of probability intervals than global calibration, across 3 tasks and 14 models, with the effect amplified when combined with global scaling.
stance_target: fine-grained/local calibration is a publishable and empirically superior approach to code-revision confidence
scope_conditions: 3 ACR tasks, 14 models of various sizes
quoted_support: fine-grained confidence scores consistently achieve lower calibration error across a broader range of probability intervals, and this effect is further amplified when global Platt-scaling is applied.

claim: The paper's notion of 'fine-grained' confidence is per-edit/per-hunk local decision calibration via post-hoc recalibration of output confidence scores, not a hidden-state probe and not decomposed per functional requirement or test case.
stance_target: granularity and mechanism used differ from a hidden-state probing approach to per-requirement code correctness
quoted_support: correctness is often determined by local edit decisions and miscalibration can be sample-dependent, thereby motivating fine-grained confidence calibration
